name: team_planning_set_position
description: Open a position in a scenario of a Team Planning plan, or change or reopen one by passing its position_id. A position is a framework role and one of that role's levels (the level pay bands key on), in a unit, at an FTE above 0 and at most 1. basis 'backfill' is committed budget; 'new' is planned. cost_centre is the position's own label, which decides its open seat and any occupant the plan changes, ahead of the cost_centre rules; an occupant the plan leaves alone keeps their own. Omit it to leave the position to the rules, which clears any label it had. hiring_status is not_started (the default), recruiting, on_hold (recruiting paused: the seat is empty and gets no forecast start) or offer_accepted, which needs a target_start. target_start is the date the seat is filled from; without one, an open seat is forecast to start the unit's time_to_hire rule after it opens. Give every field each time: the scenario's position becomes exactly this. Steps after the scenario, and its alternatives, inherit it unless they change it. Refused unless the caller is one of the plan's editors. `note` is Markdown: links, **bold**, _italic_, lists and `code` render, a bare URL becomes a link, typed HTML shows as text and images render as links.

note.description: Why this is in the plan, such as the business reason for a move. Optional, at most 2000 characters; it never changes what the scenario resolves to. A note on a change to a person goes when they are forgotten. Any other note, such as one on a unit, a position or a rule, stays until the plan is deleted, so keep personal details out of it.

scenario_id.description: The scenario, or the plan's id for the baseline.

position_id.description: Omit to open a new position.
